prompt: What is the **area** of the rectangle below? Give your answer in **square centimeters**.

diagram.alt: Rectangle 8 centimeters wide and 5 centimeters tall

hint: Area tells how many unit squares cover the rectangle. Which two measurements on the picture do you multiply?
explanation: Read the side lengths from the picture: the rectangle is $8$ cm long and $5$ cm tall.
A rectangle can be filled with rows of unit squares, so its area is length times width: $8 \times 5$.
Think of $5$ rows with $8$ squares in each row, which gives $8 \times 5 = 40$ squares.
The area of the rectangle is $40$ square centimeters.

alternativeExplanations.title: Count the unit squares
steps: Picture the rectangle covered by a grid of squares that are each $1$ cm by $1$ cm.
Every row holds $8$ of these squares, and the height of $5$ cm makes $5$ rows.
Add the rows one at a time: $8 + 8 + 8 + 8 + 8 = 40$ squares.
Each square is one square centimeter, so the area is $40$ square centimeters.

alternativeExplanations.title: Why "square" centimeters?
steps: Multiplying $8$ cm by $5$ cm multiplies the units as well as the numbers: cm $\times$ cm gives cm².
A length only measures along a line, but an area covers a flat region, so it needs **square** units.
Putting the number and the unit together gives $8 \text{ cm} \times 5 \text{ cm} = 40 \text{ cm}^2$, which is $40$ square centimeters.

hints.text: Area tells how many unit squares cover the rectangle. Which two measurements on the picture do you multiply?
Read the labels on the picture: the rectangle is $8$ cm long and $5$ cm tall. Multiply length by width, so work out $8 \times 5$.
$8 \times 5 = 40$, so the area of the rectangle is $40$ square centimeters.
